newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks pull back at close, eye Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks pull back at close, eye Wall Street.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended lower on Monday with a slide in early New York trade pushing the bourse into profit-taking, dealers said.

Endesa was the notable exception, although dealers said they were unaware of what specifically was pushing the stock higher. Some speculated that the only explanation for such a sharp rise could be position-taking ahead of the upcoming privatisation.
The general index shed 3.96 points, 0.66 percent, to 600.62 and the Ibex fell 54.86 points, 0.79 percent, to 6,884.56.
Repsol shed 30 pesetas, off an early high of 6,390 pesetas after the Industry Ministry said it was removing the LPG price freeze, seen boosting year-end results, analysts said.

Gas Natural overturned initial sharp gains after the government approved an around one percent fall in the domestic tariff and an up to three percent fall in the industrial tariff. The shares eventually closed down 240 pesetas to 32,190.

Stocks are seen testing new highs again soon, helped by the recent maturing of a special 760 billion peseta government debt issue, with much of those funds seen coming into the share market in search of higher returns.
